# A minimization approach to hyperbolic Cauchy problems

Received October 28, 2013 and in revised form March 18, 2014

**Abstract.** Developing an original idea of De Giorgi, we introduce a new and purely variational approach to the Cauchy problem for a wide class of defocusing hyperbolic equations. The main novel feature is that the solutions are obtained as limits of functions that minimize suitable functionals in spacetime (where the initial data of the Cauchy problem serve as prescribed boundary conditions). This opens up the way to new connections between the hyperbolic world and that of the calculus of variations. Also dissipative equations can be treated. Finally, we discuss several examples of equations that fit into this framework, including nonlocal equations, in particular equations with the fractional Laplacian.

**Keywords.** Nonlinear hyperbolic equations, minimization, a priori estimates

• Other equations. Just to make an example, what about

\[
w''-\frac{2}{q}\,\mathrm{div}\big(|\nabla w|^{q-2}\nabla w\big)+\frac{p}{2}|w|^{p-2}w=0,
\]

the wave equation for the \(q\)-Laplacian with defocusing nonlinearity?
This would correspond to the functional

\[
\int_0^\infty \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} e^{-t/\varepsilon}\big(\varepsilon^2|v'|^2+|\nabla v|^q+|v|^p\big)\,dx\,dt.
\]

As far as we know, even the existence of global weak solutions (to the Cauchy problem) for large \(q\) is unknown. Does the method of De Giorgi work to solve this problem?

• The abstract form of De Giorgi’s Conjecture. Consider any convex functional of the Calculus of Variations,

\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u,\ldots)\,dx
\]

Let \(v_\varepsilon(t,x)\) be the minimizer of

\[
\int_0^\infty e^{-t/\varepsilon}\left(\int_\Omega \varepsilon^2|v_\varepsilon''(t,\cdot)|^2\,dx+F(v_\varepsilon(t,\cdot))\right)\,dt
\]

with given boundary conditions \(v_\varepsilon(0,\cdot)\) and \(v'_\varepsilon(0,\cdot)\).
As \(\varepsilon\to 0\), does \(v_\varepsilon\) converge to some \(w\), which solves the Cauchy Problem for the equation

\[
w''+\nabla F(w)=0\quad ?
\]

Title: On stable solutions for boundary reactions: a De Giorgi-type result in dimension 4+1
Authors: Alessio Figalli, Joaquim Serra
Date: Mon May  8 08:51:27 2017

We prove that every bounded stable solution of \[ (-\Delta)^{1/2} u + f(u) =0 \qquad \mbox{in }\mathbb R^3\] is a 1D profile, i.e., $u(x)= \phi(e\cdot x)$ for some $e\in \mathbb S^2$, where $\phi:\mathbb R\to \mathbb R$ is a nondecreasing bounded stable solution in dimension one. This proves the De Giorgi conjecture in dimension $4$ for the half-Laplacian. Equivalently, we give a positive answer to the De Giorgi conjecture for boundary reactions in $\mathbb R^{d+1}_+=\mathbb R^{d+1}\cap \{x_{d+1}\geq 0\}$ when $d = 4$, by proving that all critical points of $$ \int_{\{x_{d+1\geq 0}\}} \frac12 |\nabla U|^2 \,dx\, dx_{d+1} + \int_{\{x_{d+1}=0\}} \frac 1 4 (1-U^2)^2 \,dx $$ that are monotone in $\mathbb R^d$ (that is, up to a rotation, $\partial_{x_d} U>0$) are one dimensional. Our result is analogue to the fact that stable embedded minimal surfaces in $\mathbb R^3$ are planes. Note that the corresponding result about stable solutions to the classical Allen-Cahn equation (namely, when the half-Laplacian is replaced by the classical Laplacian) is still open.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Authors:Virginia Agostiniani, Chiara Bernardini

View PDF HTML (experimental)

> Abstract:We prove a rigidity result for the problem $\Delta_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $\Sigma$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $\Sigma$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.
